title: Past North Pacific pressure cut monthly PDO test error by 6.15% in 1981-2025
abstract: We tested whether past North Pacific pressure adds monthly PDO prediction skill after prior PDO and Nino 3.4 are known. Earlier-year fits gave 540 test months in 1981-2025. Pressure at lags one and two reduced mean squared error from 0.323442 to 0.303558, a 6.15% reduction with a conditional 95% five-year block interval of 2.70% to 9.47%. Adding target-month pressure gave a larger 23.17% reduction. Rolling fits and a stronger ocean-history base retained past-pressure gains of 5.92% and 6.41%. This separates a short-lead benefit from the larger concurrent reconstruction benefit in earlier campaign work. Data overlap with that work. Revised indices, assumed immediate data access, simple models, repeated tests and conditional intervals limit inference. This is not measured operational skill or a causal test. Code, exact source hashes, aggregate evidence, audits and a figure are included; external monthly records stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Past and concurrent pressure gave different monthly PDO error reductions on matched 1981-2025 targets. Lines show conditional 95% five-year block intervals. Concurrent pressure is not a forecast input.
